challenge.better_approach: The orchestrator's literal wording (any change inside a closure reseals the proof) re-runs users' proofs on a tool change: that reopens item 7 and its measured cost (55 proofs/19 components, 30+ min). A pre-merge-commit reseal was measured in a scratch repo: git add inside the hook does not land in the --no-ff merge commit, so it cannot carry a reseal. Making the 70 ownerless proofs obey the same owner rule as the 723 owned ones is the smallest change that removes the cause.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That every ownerless proof's home carries its own charter, measured 2026-11-16: bin/, press_office/ and all 13 skills/<s>/ hold intention+why.json. And that the 70 standing whole-closure seals narrow on their next reseal; until then they still name foreign files, so the walk reseals them once.
challenge.prior_art: 3e80b61b7acf (reseal by owner) and 184d211153ff (closure stops at the component) are the rule; both use address.component_of, which returns None outside cairn/{tools,machines,devices}, and 184d's docstring keeps the whole closure for 'a proof under no component'. validation_store.component_root_for is already the seal's address rule (<home>/proofs/<stem>.py -> <home>). 143e3974647b and 86b6bf19ed2a are neighbours; none covers ownerless proofs.
challenge.real_collision: address.component_of is not widened: its callers (encapsulation sieve, roster) define a component as cairn-rung directories, and the distinction is recorded — a home is a seal's owner, not a roster component.

answers.falsifier: Done when a closure taken for skills/sail/proofs/test_sail_door.py over a raw list naming cairn/machines/learning_block/learning_block.py drops it, a staged skills/sail/door.py selects test_sail_door under a closure seal and a pre-closure seal, a staged learning_block.py selects no skill proof, and a component's own reach is unchanged. Wrong intent if a skill proof's correctness genuinely depends on tool files it imports such that narrowing hides a real break (then the close is right to red and the fix is the land reselecting).
answers.how: validation_store._owned_by_the_proofs_component: when component_of(proof) is None, the owner is component_root_for(proof) and the closure keeps only ownerless files under it. reseal.proofs_touching: a staged file with no component is owned by the deepest census home holding it, and that home's proofs are selected. Red-first proof in cairn/devices/tester/proofs replays test_sail_door and test_sorted_probes.
answers.shape: aside — a fix to the stale-seal refusals that cost 40e4 (q147) and 6095 (q164) a walk each
answers.traces_to: Law 9 (a seal that went stale with nothing able to reseal it reds a later, unrelated ticket's close) and Akien's 2026-10-05 answer 'tool proofs: agreed' (foreground-decisions item 7): a home's proofs re-run on its own change, never on a tool's.
answers.what: A proof that sits outside cairn/{tools,machines,devices} (under skills/, bin/ or press_office/) belongs to its home, the directory holding its proofs/, so its seal's closure stops at that home and a commit touching the home reseals it, exactly as a component's proofs are handled.

bullets.text: 70 of 793 seals are ownerless (31 bin, 2 press_office, 37 across 13 skills); proofs_touching drops a staged file whose owner is None, so these proofs never resealed at commit, not even for their own door.py
